company wants to view all clusters and workloads from a central location.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.
incorrectAnswers: Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.
Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.
Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.
explanation:
EKS Connector lets you register on-premises and other conformant clusters so their status, configuration and workloads show in the EKS console alongside EKS clusters. The other options do not provide a native central cluster/workload view without significant extra setup.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-connector.html

factChecks.explanation: Amazon EKS Connector registers any conformant Kubernetes cluster (including on-premises) so it appears with status and workloads in the EKS console. question:
A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the
ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from
database administrators.
Which solution meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
incorrectAnswers: Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.
explanation:
Client-side encryption encrypts data in the application before it is written to RDS, so database administrators only see ciphertext. Server-side or volume encryption protects data at rest but is transparently decrypted for anyone with access to the service or instance.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.Keys.html

factChecks.explanation: EBS encryption plus instance role does not protect data from DBAs/OS admins (and no database is even specified). Client-side encryption with KMS keeps data encrypted before it reaches the database, hiding it from database administrators.

migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company's applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale

Which migration solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.
explanation:
Aurora MySQL keeps MySQL compatibility and Aurora Auto Scaling adds or removes Aurora Replicas as demand changes. Redshift and DynamoDB break application compatibility, and RDS storage scaling does not add compute capacity.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Integrating.AutoScaling.html

factChecks.explanation: RDS storage autoscaling does not scale compute. Aurora (MySQL-compatible) migrated with DMS and Aurora Auto Scaling for replicas is the expected answer.

A company wants to use an event-driven programming model with AWS Lambda. The company wants to reduce startup latency for Lambda
functions that run on Java 11. The company does not have strict latency requirements for the applications. The company wants to reduce cold
starts and outlier latencies when a function scales up.

correctAnswer: Configure Lambda SnapStart.
incorrectAnswers: Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency.
Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions.
Increase the memory of the Lambda functions.
explanation:
SnapStart snapshots the initialized execution environment and resumes from it, reducing cold-start and outlier latency for Java at no additional cost, whereas provisioned concurrency is billed continuously and is meant for strict latency requirements. Timeout does not affect startup time.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/snapstart.html

factChecks.explanation: Provisioned concurrency incurs continuous charges and is for strict latency needs. With no strict latency requirement and Java 11, Lambda SnapStart (no extra cost for Java) is the cost-effective way to cut cold starts and outlier latencies. Note the Java 11 runtime itself is deprecated; current SnapStart supports Java 11+ (Java 17/21 preferred).

question:
A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such
as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive
information.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.
incorrectAnswers: Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.
Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.
Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.
explanation:
Lake Formation data filters grant SELECT with column-level, row-level or cell-level restrictions on Data Catalog tables, hiding sensitive portions without custom code. A plain IAM role grants whole-table access, and Lambda scrubbing adds operational overhead.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/data-filtering.html

factChecks.explanation: An IAM role granting access to Lake Formation tables does not hide portions of data. Lake Formation data filters provide column-, row- and cell-level security with least operational overhead.

question:
A company deploys Amazon EC2 instances that run in a VPC. The EC2 instances load source data into Amazon S3 buckets so that the data can be
processed in the future. According to compliance laws, the data must not be transmitted over the public internet. Servers in the company's on-
premises data center will consume the output from an application that runs on the EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and the VPC.
incorrectAnswers: Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
Set up an AWS Transit Gateway connection from the VPC to the S3 buckets. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
Set up proxy EC2 instances that have routes to NAT gateways. Configure the proxy EC2 instances to fetch S3 data and feed the application instances.
explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint keeps EC2-to-S3 traffic on the AWS network, and Direct Connect gives on-premises servers a private path to the VPC. An interface endpoint for EC2 does not carry S3 traffic, and NAT proxies use the public internet.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html

factChecks.explanation: Key uses an interface endpoint for Amazon EC2, which does nothing for EC2-to-S3 traffic. The gateway S3 endpoint plus Direct Connect keeps traffic off the public internet.

question:
A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information
from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint. Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.
incorrectAnswers: Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway. Update the application to use the new internet gateway.
Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection. Update the application to use the new VPN connection.
Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway. Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.
explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint lets private-subnet instances reach S3 without an internet gateway or NAT, and bucket policies can restrict access with aws:sourceVpce. IGW/NAT use the internet path.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed internet gateway contradicts 'must not use the internet'. A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 keeps traffic on the AWS network.

question:
A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in
the Kubernetes secrets object. The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
incorrectAnswers: Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
explanation:
EKS natively supports envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets with a KMS key, requiring no code changes. Encrypting in the application, a Lambda function or Parameter Store adds work and does not encrypt the Kubernetes secrets object itself.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/enable-kms.html

factChecks.explanation: Application-level encryption is highest overhead. Enabling secrets encryption with a KMS key on the EKS cluster is the expected answer (note: for Kubernetes 1.28+ EKS envelope-encrypts secrets by default, so the question is somewhat dated).

question:
A company is designing a new multi-tier web application that consists of the following components:
• Web and application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances as part of Auto Scaling groups
• An Amazon RDS DB instance for data storage
A solutions architect needs to limit access to the application servers so that only the web servers can access them.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
incorrectAnswers: Deploy AWS PrivateLink in front of the application servers. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
Deploy a VPC endpoint in front of the application servers. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
explanation:
A security group can reference the web tier's security group as its source, so only web servers can reach the application servers, and an ALB distributes traffic across the Auto Scaling group. Network ACLs are stateless subnet-level rules that cannot reference instances dynamically.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-benefits.html

factChecks.explanation: PrivateLink plus NACL is not the standard answer. Place the app tier behind an ALB and use a security group allowing only the web tier. ALB option with security group is correct.

question:
A company runs a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application has a microservices
architecture. The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a
centralized location.
Which solution meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
incorrectAnswers: Run AWS App Mesh in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the App Mesh console.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to capture data events. Query CloudTrail by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.
Run the Amazon CloudWatch agent in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
explanation:
Container Insights collects, aggregates and summarizes metrics and logs from containerized microservices on EKS into CloudWatch. App Mesh is a service mesh and CloudTrail records API calls, not application metrics and logs.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights.html

factChecks.explanation: Container Insights is the purpose-built feature that collects, aggregates and summarizes metrics and logs for EKS; keyed plain agent option is defensible but less direct.

question:
A company has deployed its newest product on AWS. The product runs in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer. The company
stores the product’s objects in an Amazon S3 bucket.
The company recently experienced malicious attacks against its systems. The company needs a solution that continuously monitors for malicious
activity in the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns to the S3 bucket. The solution must also report suspicious activity and display the
information on a dashboard.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor and report findings to AWS Security Hub.
incorrectAnswers: Configure Amazon Macie to monitor and report findings to AWS Config.
Configure Amazon Inspector to monitor and report findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Configure AWS Config to monitor and report findings to Amazon EventBridge.
explanation:
GuardDuty continuously monitors CloudTrail, VPC flow, DNS and S3 data events for malicious activity, and its findings aggregate in AWS Security Hub for a dashboard view. Macie discovers sensitive data and does not report findings to AWS Config.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/what-is-guardduty.html

factChecks.explanation: Continuous threat detection for account, workloads, S3 access with dashboard/reporting = GuardDuty with findings to Security Hub. Macie is S3 sensitive data discovery, not threat detection.

question:
A company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for its Amazon EC2 instances that have an SMB file share mounted as a volume in
the us-east-1 Region. The company has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes for planned system maintenance or unplanned service
disruptions. The company needs to replicate the file system to the us-west-2 Region. The replicated data must not be deleted by any user for 5
years.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
incorrectAnswers: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
explanation:
Multi-AZ file systems fail over automatically to a standby AZ during maintenance or disruption, meeting the 5-minute RPO that Single-AZ cannot guarantee. Vault Lock in compliance mode makes the vault immutable so even privileged users cannot delete backups; governance mode can be removed by users with IAM permissions.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html

factChecks.explanation: RPO of 5 minutes through planned maintenance and unplanned disruptions requires Multi-AZ FSx for Windows (automatic failover, high availability); Single-AZ file systems tolerate loss of availability/data updates since last backup. Compliance mode (not governance) is needed so no user can delete.

question:
A solutions architect is designing a security solution for a company that wants to provide developers with individual AWS accounts through AWS
Organizations, while also maintaining standard security controls. Because the individual developers will have AWS account root user-level access
to their own accounts, the solutions architect wants to ensure that the mandatory AWS CloudTrail configuration that is applied to new developer
accounts is not modified.
Which action meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create a service control policy (SCP) that prohibits changes to CloudTrail, and attach it to the developer accounts.
incorrectAnswers: Create an IAM policy that prohibits changes to CloudTrail, and attach it to the root user.
Create a new trail in CloudTrail from within the developer accounts with the organization trails option enabled.
Create a service-linked role for CloudTrail with a policy condition that allows changes only from an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the management account.
explanation:
SCPs set maximum permissions for member accounts, including their root users. IAM policies cannot be attached to the root user, and organization trails are created from the management account.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer is wrong. You cannot attach IAM policies to the root user. An SCP attached to member accounts restricts even the member account's root user, so the SCP option (currently a distractor) is correct. The explanation quotes unrelated condition-key text.

question:
A company is planning to deploy a business-critical application in the AWS Cloud. The application requires durable storage with consistent, low-
latency performance.
Which type of storage should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
incorrectAnswers: Instance store volume
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
Throughput Optimized HDD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
explanation:
Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes are persistent and designed for consistent, low-latency I/O in critical workloads. Instance store data is lost when the instance stops or fails, Memcached is an in-memory cache without persistence, and Throughput Optimized HDD targets throughput, not low latency.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volume-types.html

factChecks.explanation: Instance store is temporary and not durable. Provisioned IOPS SSD EBS gives durable, consistent low latency.

question:
A company uses Amazon API Gateway to manage its REST APIs that third-party service providers access. The company must protect the REST
APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks.
What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure AWS WAF.
incorrectAnswers: Configure AWS Shield.
Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS Shield in CloudFront.
Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS WAF in CloudFront.
explanation:
AWS WAF web ACLs can be associated directly with API Gateway REST API stages to block SQL injection and XSS; adding CloudFront is extra work. Shield addresses DDoS.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html

factChecks.explanation: Shield does not block SQLi/XSS; AWS WAF associated directly with the API Gateway stage does, and is the most operationally efficient.

question:
A company wants to provide users with access to AWS resources. The company has 1,500 users and manages their access to on-premises
resources through Active Directory user groups on the corporate network. However, the company does not want users to have to maintain another
identity to access the resources. A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on-
premises resources.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
incorrectAnswers: Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.
Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.
Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
explanation:
SAML federation lets AD users sign in with existing credentials and assume IAM roles mapped to their groups, with no new IAM identities. IAM users create separate identities, Cognito user pools do not use AD groups for AWS resource access, and cross-account roles are for accounts.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_saml.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer (IAM user per person) contradicts the requirement of no separate identity. SAML 2.0 federation with roles mapped to AD groups is correct.

question:
A company is hosting a website behind multiple Application Load Balancers. The company has different distribution rights for its content around
the world. A solutions architect needs to ensure that users are served the correct content without violating distribution rights.
Which configuration should the solutions architect choose to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation policy
incorrectAnswers: Configure Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF.
Configure Application Load Balancers with AWS WAF
Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geoproximity routing policy
explanation:
Geolocation routing directs DNS queries to a chosen endpoint based on the user's country or continent, which lets each region be served only the content it is licensed for. Geoproximity routes by physical distance and bias, and WAF or CloudFront geo restrictions only block, not select content.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geo.html

factChecks.explanation: Serving the correct content per region without violating distribution rights is geolocation routing: Route 53 geolocation records send users in each location to the matching ALB. CloudFront geographic restrictions apply to the whole distribution (allow/deny) and WAF only blocks or allows, neither serves different content per location. Route 53 geoproximity routes by distance, not rights boundaries

question:
A company stores its data on premises. The amount of data is growing beyond the company's available capacity.
The company wants to migrate its data from the on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs a solution that will
automatically validate the integrity of the data after the transfer.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on premises. Configure the DataSync agent to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
incorrectAnswers: Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Configure the Snowball Edge device to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Configure the S3 File Gateway to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
Configure an accelerator in Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on premises. Configure the accelerator to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
explanation:
DataSync uses checksum verification during and after transfer to validate integrity for online transfers to S3. Snowball Edge is a shipped device, and Transfer Acceleration has no on-premises accelerator.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/configure-data-verification-options.html

factChecks.explanation: Snowball Edge is an offline shipped device (not 'online' transfer, and closed to new customers); DataSync does online transfer with automatic checksum integrity verification.

question:
A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to
upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions. The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost
compliance purposes.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
incorrectAnswers: Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
explanation:
Storage Lens aggregates storage metrics across all accounts in an organization and Regions, including incomplete multipart upload data, with minimal setup. SCPs only restrict permissions, Multi-Region Access Points only route requests, and Config rules evaluate configuration rather than reporting multipart upload counts.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens.html

factChecks.explanation: S3 Storage Lens gives organization-wide visibility across accounts and Regions, including incomplete multipart upload metrics, with no per-bucket rule setup. AWS Config does not report incomplete multipart upload counts, and SCPs and Multi-Region Access Points do not report anything.

question:
A company runs a production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company wants to upgrade the database version for security compliance
reasons. Because the database contains critical data, the company wants a quick solution to upgrade and test functionality without losing any
data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Use Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments to deploy and test production changes.
incorrectAnswers: Create an RDS manual snapshot. Upgrade to the new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
Use native backup and restore. Restore the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
explanation:
Blue/Green Deployments create a synchronized staging copy where you can upgrade the engine version and test, then promote it with typically under a minute of downtime and no data loss. A snapshot plus in-place upgrade gives no test environment.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/blue-green-deployments.html

factChecks.explanation: Key (snapshot then in-place upgrade) does not allow testing before cutover; RDS Blue/Green Deployments is the purpose-built, lowest-overhead way to upgrade and test.

question:
A solutions architect is creating a data processing job that runs once daily and can take up to 2 hours to complete. If the job is interrupted, it has
to restart from the beginning.
How should the solutions architect address this issue in the MOST cost-effective manner?
correctAnswer: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Fargate task triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
incorrectAnswers: Create a script that runs locally on an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance that is triggered by a cron job.
Create an AWS Lambda function triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task running on Amazon EC2 triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
explanation:
A scheduled Fargate task runs only for the roughly 2 hours needed and is charged for that time, with no servers to keep running. Lambda times out at 15 minutes, and a reserved or ECS-on-EC2 instance costs money while idle.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html

factChecks.explanation: Job runs 2 hours daily; an always-on Reserved EC2 instance wastes about 22 hours. A Fargate task on a schedule is billed only while running and has no 15-minute limit (Lambda cannot run 2 hours).

question:
A social media company wants to store its database of user profiles, relationships, and interactions in the AWS Cloud. The company needs an
application to monitor any changes in the database. The application needs to analyze the relationships between the data entities and to provide
recommendations to users.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
incorrectAnswers: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
explanation:
Neptune is a graph database suited to relationship analysis and recommendations, and Neptune Streams natively captures every graph change in order. QLDB is a ledger database, not a graph store.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/streams.html

factChecks.explanation: Neptune Streams is the native, managed change-capture for Neptune; Kinesis Data Streams is not a Neptune change feed, and QLDB is not a graph DB (and QLDB is retired).

question:

Amazon EC2 Linux instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The needed amount of storage space will continue to grow for

question:
A company runs a website that stores images of historical events. Website users need the ability to search and view images based on the year
that the event in the image occurred. On average, users request each image only once or twice a year. The company wants a highly available
solution to store and deliver the images to users.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.
incorrectAnswers: Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
explanation:
S3 Standard-IA stores data across multiple AZs at lower per-GB cost, ideal when each image is requested once or twice a year, and S3 serves it without servers. EBS/EFS with EC2 cost far more.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html

factChecks.explanation: Rarely accessed images with high availability: S3 Standard-IA static website is cheapest. EBS+EC2 is the most expensive and not highly available.

question:
A company has multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations that different business units use. The company has multiple
offices around the world. The company needs to update security group rules to allow new office CIDR ranges or to remove old CIDR ranges across
the organization. The company wants to centralize the management of security group rules to minimize the administrative overhead that updating
CIDR ranges requires.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Create a VPC customer managed prefix list that contains the list of CIDRs. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the prefix list across the organization. Use the prefix list in the security groups across the organization.
incorrectAnswers: Create VPC security groups in the organization's management account. Update the security groups when a CIDR range update is necessary.

Create an AWS managed prefix list. Use an AWS Security Hub policy to enforce the security group update across the organization. Use an AWS Lambda function to update the prefix list automatically when the CIDR ranges change.

Create security groups in a central administrative AWS account. Create an AWS Firewall Manager common security group policy for the whole organization. Select the previously created security groups as primary groups in the policy.
explanation:
A customer-managed prefix list can be shared with other accounts via AWS RAM, and updating it updates every security group that references it. AWS-managed prefix lists cannot be modified or shared, and Firewall Manager adds cost.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/managed-prefix-lists.html

factChecks.explanation: Security groups are per-VPC and cannot be centrally created in the management account for all accounts. A customer-managed prefix list shared via AWS RAM is the right centralized, low-cost mechanism.

question:
A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. Application peak hours occur at the same time
each day. Application users report slow application performance at the start of peak hours. The application performs normally 2-3 hours after
peak hours begin. The company wants to ensure that the application works properly at the start of peak hours.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances before peak hours.
incorrectAnswers: Configure an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic properly to the instances.
Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on memory utilization.
Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on CPU utilization.
explanation:
Scheduled scaling increases capacity at a known time, so instances are already running when the predictable daily peak begins. Dynamic policies only react after metrics rise, which causes the observed slowness at the start of peak hours.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed ALB answer does nothing for capacity lag (a load balancer spreads load but adds no instances). Peak at the same time each day with slow start means scheduled scaling before peak hours. Dynamic scaling reacts too late.

question:
A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and at peak
times of the year. The company wants to scale the database more effectively for its applications that connect to the database.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
incorrectAnswers: Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.
explanation:
RDS Proxy is a managed service that pools and shares database connections so applications can scale without overwhelming the database, with no code changes beyond the endpoint. DynamoDB is a different database, and a custom EC2 proxy adds operational overhead.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html

factChecks.explanation: Key (DynamoDB with connection pooling) is invalid; RDS Proxy is the managed connection-pooling answer for an RDS database.

question:
A company uses AWS Cost Explorer to monitor its AWS costs. The company notices that Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage and
snapshot costs increase every month. However, the company does not purchase additional EBS storage every month. The company wants to
optimize monthly costs for its current storage usage.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Delete all nonessential snapshots. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create and manage the snapshots according to the company's snapshot policy requirements.
incorrectAnswers: Use logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to monitor the storage utilization of Amazon EBS. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
Use a custom script to monitor space usage. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
Delete all expired and unused snapshots to reduce snapshot costs.
explanation:
Costs grow because snapshots accumulate; Data Lifecycle Manager automates snapshot retention with little overhead. Elastic Volumes can increase size but not decrease it, and a one-time delete does not stop the growth.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/requesting-ebs-volume-modifications.html

factChecks.explanation: Key relies on shrinking EBS volumes with Elastic Volumes, which is not supported (size can only increase). Deleting unneeded snapshots and automating with Data Lifecycle Manager is the answer.

question:

Amazon S3 bucket that contains assets for the application, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database that contains the dataset for the application.

correctAnswer: Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon RDS for MySQL. Update the RDS for MySQL security group to allow access from only the subnets that the ECS cluster will generate tasks in. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from only the S3 VPC endpoint.
incorrectAnswers: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the KMS key policy includes encrypt and decrypt permissions for the ECS task execution role.

question:
A company has customers located across the world. The company wants to use automation to secure its systems and network infrastructure. The
company's security team must be able to track and audit all incremental changes to the infrastructure.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
explanation:
CloudFormation provisions infrastructure through code and Config records and audits configuration changes over time. Organizations does not build infrastructure and Service Catalog does not track configuration changes.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html

factChecks.explanation: AWS Organizations manages accounts, not infrastructure provisioning; CloudFormation automates infrastructure and AWS Config records and audits configuration changes. Stem has corruption (traffick means track).

question:
A company is moving its data and applications to AWS during a multiyear migration project. The company wants to securely access data on
Amazon S3 from the company's AWS Region and from the company's on-premises location. The data must not traverse the internet. The company
has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its Region and its on-premises location.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the interface endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
incorrectAnswers: Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the gateway endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
Create a gateway in AWS Transit Gateway to access Amazon S3 securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to access the data securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
explanation:
Gateway endpoints do not allow access from on-premises networks; interface endpoints (PrivateLink) are reachable over Direct Connect via private IPs.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html

factChecks.explanation: Gateway endpoints cannot be used from on-premises (Direct Connect, VPN, TGW); interface endpoints are required.

question:
A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for the company's development teams. The
development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications,
the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources that are created.
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag
has an approved value.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.
incorrectAnswers: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
explanation:
Tag policies define allowed tag keys and values for accounts in an organization and can be enforced for supported resource types. Resource Groups only reports compliance, and the IAM options do not centrally validate approved values.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies.html

factChecks.explanation: Approved tag values across accounts is the job of an Organizations tag policy (with enforcement). The keyed IAM group policy only requires a tag be present, not that it be an approved value, and is per-account.

question:
A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company wants a secure solution to manage the master user password by
rotating the password every 30 days.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
incorrectAnswers: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
explanation:
Secrets Manager integrates natively with RDS to store and automatically rotate the master password on a schedule you set (e.g. 30 days). Custom Lambda or CLI changes need extra build and maintenance, and Parameter Store cannot rotate RDS passwords.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rds-secrets-manager.html

factChecks.explanation: RDS integration with Secrets Manager (managed master user password) rotates the secret automatically; custom Lambda is more overhead and Parameter Store has no native RDS rotation.

question:
A company performs tests on an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table. The tests run for 4 hours once a week. The company knows
how many read and write operations the application performs to the table each second during the tests. The company does not currently use
DynamoDB for any other use case. A solutions architect needs to optimize the costs for the table.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Choose on-demand mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
incorrectAnswers: Choose provisioned mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 1-year term.
Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 3-year term.
explanation:
On-demand mode is pay-per-request, so the table costs nothing while idle outside the 4-hour weekly test. Provisioned capacity and reserved capacity bill continuously and suit steady, predictable use.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/capacity-mode.html

factChecks.explanation: Key on-demand is reasonable for a weekly 4-hour workload with no cost when idle (provisioned mode bills hourly for provisioned capacity; reserved capacity needs steady use). Option text 'update the read and write capacity units' is incoherent for on-demand. Explanation unrelated.

question:
A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company performs periodic financial assessments of its AWS costs. The
company recently identified unusual spending.
The company needs a solution to prevent unusual spending. The solution must monitor costs and notify responsible stakeholders in the event of
unusual spending.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
incorrectAnswers: Use an AWS Budgets template to create a zero spend budget.
Create AWS Pricing Calculator estimates for the current running workload pricing details.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor costs and to identify unusual spending.
explanation:
Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to detect unusual spend and alerts stakeholders by email or SNS. A zero spend budget only signals any spend and Pricing Calculator only estimates.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html

factChecks.explanation: A zero spend budget only alerts when spending exceeds $0; AWS Cost Anomaly Detection is the service for detecting and notifying on unusual spend.

question:
A marketing company receives a large amount of new clickstream data in Amazon S3 from a marketing campaign. The company needs to analyze
the clickstream data in Amazon S3 quickly. Then the company needs to determine whether to process the data further in the data pipeline.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Athena to query the data.
incorrectAnswers: Create external tables in a Spark catalog. Configure jobs in AWS Glue to query the data.
Create external tables in a Hive metastore. Configure Spark jobs in Amazon EMR to query the data.
Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to use SQL to query the data.
explanation:
A Glue crawler populates the Data Catalog and Athena runs serverless SQL directly on S3 with nothing to manage. Glue jobs and EMR require authoring and running jobs or clusters, and Flink targets streaming data.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html

factChecks.explanation: Quick ad hoc analysis of S3 data with least overhead: Glue crawler + serverless Athena. Glue Spark jobs or EMR add work; Kinesis analytics is streaming.
